chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, that one of our companions wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Mazi (peace be upon him) asking him about the prayer upon glass, and he said:

So when my letter reached him, I thought and said to myself, 'It is from what the earth produces, and it is not for me to ask him about it.' He said, so he wrote to me: 'Do not pray upon glass, and even if your soul tells you that it is from what the earth produces, it is from salt and sand, and both have been metamorphosed.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer or prostration (sajdah) in this context

ai.seo_question: Is glass considered valid for prostration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle of distinguishing between natural earth produce and processed materials, specifically addressing the status of glass. The Imam clarifies that despite its earthly origins, glass is considered 'metamorphosed' (masukh) from salt and sand, rendering it unsuitable for sajdah. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the purity and natural state of materials used in worship, distinguishing them from man-made or altered substances.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn that, ‘One of our companions wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazyasws (7th Imamasws) asking himasws about the Salāt upon the glass. He said:

‘So when my letter was implemented to go to himasws, I thought and said (to myself), ‘It (glass) is from what the earth grows and it is not for me that I should be asking himasws about it’. So heasws wrote to me: ‘You cannot pray Salāt upon the glass, and that you discussed it with yourself (thought about), it is from what the earth grows, but, it is from the salt and the sand, and they have both been metamorphosed’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy al-Naysaburiy from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Sajdah (prostration) on wet growing items. He (the Imam) said, ‘If your forehead touches the ground it is not harmful.’ I asked about stationary grass on the ground and dry leaves while he touches the ground. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
